# AERIS-10N hardware upgrade path — cost-efficient capability

**Provisional; modeled placeholders + real datasheet specs.** Generated by
`matlab/aeris_upgrade_trade.m`. Baseline = a CN0566-class node with its weak
reference illuminator (~2 W eff), 8×16 patch, ADL8107 LNA (1.43 dB cascade NF),
Pluto SDR. Reliable range ~1.06 km on 0.03 m².

## Real components (priced Sep 2026, single-unit)

| part | spec | price |
|---|---|---|
| Qorvo **QPA1010D** | 7.9–11 GHz GaN, 15 W, 38% PAE, 18 dB; VD **24 V**, IDQ 600 mA | ~$198 |
| Qorvo **QPA1011D** | 7.9–11 GHz GaN, 25 W, 37% PAE, 20 dB; IDQ ~1200 mA | ~$300 |
| Qorvo **CMD197** | GaAs driver, 1–24 GHz, 16 dB, +22 dBm OP1dB | ~$374 |
| **bladeRF 2.0** | AD9361, 61 MHz BW (vs Pluto 20 MHz) | ~$540 |
| +8 patches + 2× ADAR1000 | 8→16 az elements | ~$400 est |

## Trade study

| upgrade | range | +range | +$ | +avg W | km/$100 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| baseline (CN0566) | 1.06 km | — | — | — | — |
| **PA 15 W + driver** | **1.75 km** | +0.69 | $650 | 19 | **0.11** |
| PA 15 W drain-pulsed | 1.75 km | +0.69 | $750 | 6 | 0.09 |
| PA 25 W + driver | 1.99 km | +0.93 | $760 | 35 | 0.12 |
| SDR AD9361 (bladeRF) | 1.06 km | +0 (resolution) | $540 | 2 | — |
| +8 az elements | 1.50 km | +0.44 | $400 | 8 | 0.11 |
| PA 15 W + 16-el (combo) | **2.48 km** | +1.42 | $1,050 | 27 | 0.14 |

## Findings

**The GaN PA is the highest-leverage upgrade** — the QPA1010D roughly doubles
range from the weak-illuminator baseline. But three datasheet realities correct
a naive "just add a PA":

1. **The driver is the hidden cost.** The PA needs +24 dBm of drive; the
   beamformer won't provide it, so a driver (CMD197, ~$374) is required — nearly
   2× the PA's own cost. The real PA line is ~$650, not ~$200.
2. **Quiescent current dominates power, not RF.** A class-AB GaN PA burns its
   IDQ continuously (QPA1010D: 24 V × 0.6 A = 14.4 W) whether transmitting or
   not → ~17–19 W average CW-biased. **Drain-pulsing** (the datasheet's own
   mode) cuts it to ~6 W at the cost of a drain modulator — a real SWaP lever.
3. **VD = 24 V is a free integration win** — the PA runs off the same battery
   rail as the node; no separate converter. Also needs a heatsink for the 14 W
   continuous quiescent dissipation.

Other components in context:
- **More array elements** cost more for less range than the PA (gain grows
  slowly, ~+3 dB per doubling of azimuth) — a worse buy alone.
- **The SDR upgrade buys resolution and dynamic range, not range** — 30 m → 2.7 m
  range resolution and better clutter handling (helps discrimination and
  resolving closely-spaced drones), so it shows +0 km here.

## The upgraded 10N as a middle option

The **combo (PA + 16 elements ≈ $1,050, ~27 W → ~2.5 km)** takes the $6k node
to ~83% of the AERIS-10N *design* range and near the 10X's low end, for **~5% of
the 10X's cost and ~7% of its power.** Positioning:

| option | range | ~cost | ~avg power |
|---|---|---|---|
| 10N baseline | 1.1 km | $6.2k | ~40 W |
| 10N + PA | 1.75 km | $6.8k | ~60 W |
| 10N + PA + 16-el | 2.5 km | $7.2k | ~70 W |
| 10X | 6.3 km | $21.9k | 411 W |

A modestly upgraded cheap node closes much of the gap at a fraction of the
SWaP-C — the "get more out of the 10N" answer, grounded in real parts.

## Caveats

- Assumes a single PA feeding a passive array (cost-efficient). A per-element
  active array (a PA behind each patch) gives more but at N× the cost/power —
  the 10X-like design point.
- Baseline Ptpeak (~2 W) is an estimate of a real CN0566 + small driver; the
  relative ranking (PA >> array >> SDR-for-range) is robust to it.
- CMD197's +22 dBm OP1dB is marginally short of the PA's +24 dBm drive — push
  ~2 dB into compression (fine for constant-envelope LFM) or use CMD292 (+27 dBm).
